**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig traceroute engine found; against the C tools it is a testable library with an injectable transport (offline canned-packet tests on a virtual clock), partial-trace-on-transport-failure, spoof hardening (Echo Reply must come from the destination; random ident/seq; bounded run time), and it returns a structured `Trace`. **Where we are behind** (re-checked 2026-10-04): no TCP method, sequential probing only (slow on dark hops), no ECMP-aware (Paris/Dublin) strategy, RFC 5837 interface-information objects not decoded (only MPLS); ASN/reverse-DNS annotation is left to sibling modules (`dns`) (→ Backlog). Built since the survey: the UDP method, RFC 4884/4950 MPLS label stacks, interface/source/TOS/fwmark.

## Design & invariants
Pure engine behind a `Transport` seam: `traceWith` is the hop state machine over an injectable
transport (`sendFn` with TTL / `recvFn` bytes + source / `nowFn` clock), fully offline-testable from
canned packet bytes on a virtual clock; `LinuxTransport` + `trace` are the live path. Correlation over
a bounded flat slot scheme: each probe's wire sequence is `seq_base +% slot` (slot =
hop·probes_per_hop + probe); a response — even one arriving after its probe already timed out — maps
back to its slot via the ident/seq quoted inside the ICMP error (parsed by `icmp.echo.parseV4/V6`),
so late replies land in the right hop. Sequential: one probe in flight, like traceroute(8)'s default —
the state machine stays simple and every RTT is unambiguous. Hop count and probes-per-hop are bounded
(`Options.validate`; `max_probes_per_hop = 16`, `max_payload = 1024`). Allocation: `Trace` owns
exactly two slices (`hops`, `probes`), sized to the used prefix and freed by `deinit`; per-hop
`stats()` uses fixed stack scratch (via `latency-stats`). Live path is Linux + raw only: DGRAM
("ping") sockets deliver ICMP errors on the error queue, not as packets, so raw is required
(CAP_NET_RAW); per-probe TTL via setsockopt IP_TTL/IPV6_UNICAST_HOPS; ppoll for the timeout.
Clean-room from the classic traceroute(8)/mtr ICMP method (Van Jacobson's TTL-stepping applied to
ICMP Echo — a public technique) and RFC 792 ICMP formats via the sibling `icmp.echo` codec — see
NOTICE.

### A transport failure returns a partial `Trace`, not just an error

`traceWith` used to propagate a `sendFn`/`recvFn` failure with `try`, which discarded every
hop already collected — for a traceroute, eight good hops then a broken socket is most of the
answer, not a failure to report as opaquely as a caller mistake. Zig has no error payloads, so
carrying the partial result out alongside the error needed a shape decision:

- **Considered and rejected: an out-parameter** (`traceWith(gpa, t, dest, opts, partial: ?*Trace)`).
  Works, but it is a second way to receive a `Trace` bolted onto the existing one, and every
  caller — including every offline test in this file — would need to thread a pointer through
  whether or not it cares.
- **Considered and rejected: split the return into `struct { trace: Trace, err: ?TransportError }`
  with no Zig error at all.** This erases the real distinction between "a partial trace, because
  the transport broke mid-run" and "no trace at all, because `Options` were invalid or the initial
  allocation failed" — `InvalidOptions`/`OutOfMemory` happen before a single probe is sent, so
  there is nothing to hand back for them, and forcing every caller to unwrap a `Trace` value for
  those cases too would manufacture a fake one.
- **Chosen: extend `Trace` with a `transport_err: ?TransportError` field, and narrow `TraceError`
  to `error{ InvalidOptions, OutOfMemory }`.** This follows the module's own existing shape:
  `Trace` already records *how* a trace stopped as data (`reached`, `unreachable_code`), not as a
  distinct error per termination mode — a transport failure is simply a third way to stop early,
  and was the odd one out for using the `!` channel instead of a field. `sendFn`/`recvFn` failures
  are now caught inside `traceWith` (`catch |err| { transport_err = err; break :outer; }`) instead
  of propagated with `try`, so the function falls through to the same hop-packing code every other
  termination path already uses, and returns a `Trace` whose `hops`/`probes` hold whatever was
  collected up to the failure. The genuine no-partial-data cases (`InvalidOptions`, the initial
  `gpa.alloc` before any probe exists) keep the ordinary Zig error channel — nothing to carry
  alongside them either way.

**`hops_used` on a send failure.** A failure on a hop's first probe (`pi == 0`) means nothing
about that hop was ever attempted, so it is excluded from `hops_used` (set to `hi`, not `hi + 1`)
— otherwise the returned `Trace` would contain a hop whose every probe reads `.timeout` despite
none of them having been sent, indistinguishable from a hop that really was probed and got no
answer. A failure on a *later* probe of the same hop (or any `recvFn` failure, which by
definition follows a successful send) leaves `hops_used` as already set — that hop did get at
least one real attempt, the same way an `unreachable_code` stop mid-hop keeps the hop it stopped
in (see `wire.zig`'s sibling test "destination unreachable terminates and records the code").

**BREAKING for a caller that matched `TraceError`/`TransportError` on `traceWith`'s return.** A
`try traceWith(...)` or `catch |err| switch (err) { error.SendFailed, error.RecvFailed => ... }`
no longer compiles/fires for those two — the same failure now arrives as `tr.transport_err` on a
successful return. See CHANGELOG.md.

## UDP method, extensions, live options (2026-10-04)

**UDP.** Probe *k* is a datagram from the transport's bound source port (`Options.ident`, the
correlation token — the live path uses the kernel's ephemeral port, or `Options.source_port`) to `udp_port_base + k`; the
`validate` rule keeps that window inside 1…65535. A reply is an ICMP error quoting an IPv4/IPv6
header with protocol/next-header 17 and the probe's source and destination ports, with the
quoted destination equal to the trace's (the A1 F3 rule, now also for UDP). The destination's
own Port Unreachable (IPv4 code 3, IPv6 code 4) from the destination's address is `.reply` and
sets `reached`; any other Destination Unreachable — or a Port Unreachable from anyone else (A1
F1) — is terminal. The same first-answer-wins rule (A1 F12) holds. The live path sends from a
UDP socket and receives on the same raw ICMP socket as the ICMP method; a send that fails with a
pending ICMP-induced socket error (ECONNREFUSED etc., which belongs to the previous probe) is
retried once.

**Extensions (RFC 4884) and MPLS (RFC 4950).** The ICMPv4 length field (byte 5, 32-bit words;
ICMPv6 byte 4, 64-bit words) locates the extension after an original datagram of at least 128
bytes; a router predating RFC 4884 puts it at 128 bytes with the field 0, accepted only with a
version-2 header and a non-zero, verifying checksum (a zero checksum means "not computed", which
is fine only when the length field already proved an extension is there). Objects are walked by
length; class 1 / C-Type 1 entries become `MplsEntry` (label 20 bits, TC 3, S 1, TTL 8), at most
`max_mpls_labels` per probe. ICMPv4 checksums are verified before any of this (`icmpMessage`),
as `icmp.echo` does for the ICMP method.

**Live options.** `iface` → SO_BINDTODEVICE on both sockets, `source` → bind (raw socket via
`icmp.Socket`, UDP socket directly), `tos` → IP_TOS / IPV6_TCLASS on the socket that sends,
`fwmark` → SO_MARK. A live test reads them back with `getsockopt`.

## Threat model / out of scope
The live trace needs CAP_NET_RAW (raw ICMP socket). Responses are **not authenticated**: only
ident/seq quoted in the ICMP error are checked, so a spoofed router response with the right ident/seq
would be attributed to a hop (path measurement, not authentication); a response quoting a slot not
yet sent, or a slot that already has an answer, is rejected as a spoof/duplicate (A1 F5/F12 — first
non-timeout write wins a slot, not last). An Echo Reply additionally must carry the destination's own
source address to complete the trace (`reached = true`) — A1 F1: without that check, a single spoofed
Echo Reply with the right ident/seq from ANY address truncated the whole trace to one hop attributed
to the spoofer, which is a stronger claim than "path measurement" and is what the `reached` field's
own doc comment promises. `trace()` draws a fresh random ident and starting sequence per call via
`getrandom(2)` (A1 F2) rather than the raw socket's PID-derived identifier and the fixed default
`seq_base = 1` — this raises the bar against a *blind off-path* spoofer to a full unknown 16+16 bits;
it does nothing against an on-path attacker, who reads the real values off the wire. `Options.validate`
also bounds the worst-case wall time of a whole run, not just each field individually (A1 F6/F8 —
`max_run_ms`), since `max_hops`/`probes_per_hop`/`timeout_ms` each being individually bounded still
let the worst legal combination run for ~202,817 days and put ~4.2 MB on the wire toward one address
with no rate limit. Malformed/hostile ICMP bytes never panic — anything unrecognized is `.ignored` and
the probe falls through to a clean timeout (`*`); a corpus-seeded `testing.fuzz` test exercises this
directly (A1 F9).

**No destination validation (A1 F7, by design, not by oversight).** `trace`/`traceWith` accept and
probe whatever `netaddr.Ip` they are given — loopback, link-local (including the `169.254.169.254`
cloud-metadata address), private, unspecified (`0.0.0.0`) and multicast/broadcast destinations are
all accepted and probed. `netaddr` is a declared dependency and exports `isLoopback`,
`isLinkLocalUnicast`, `isPrivate`, `isMulticast`, `isUnspecified`; this module calls none of them.
For a diagnostic tool, tracing to a link-local next hop or a private-range destination is normal,
legitimate use — the previous absence of a documented stance (not the absence of the checks
themselves) was the actual gap. **A caller that exposes `trace`/`traceWith` to a destination chosen
by an untrusted party (the SSRF-shaped case) must apply its own `netaddr`-predicate validation before
calling in** — this module will not do it for them.

**Not covered by the ident/seq/source hardening above: the quoted IP header inside an ICMP error is
parsed, used to find the quoted echo header, and then discarded** (`icmp.echo.Reply.icmp_error` has
no field for the quoted destination/source/protocol) — so this module cannot compare a Time
Exceeded's or Destination Unreachable's citation against what it actually sent, only the quoted
ident+seq. That gap, and the fact that this module's receive path never verifies the ICMP checksum
(nor does the kernel, on a raw socket, before delivery), are `icmp` module findings
(`icmp`'s F2/F7 — A1 audit) shared with `pathmtu` and `icmp`'s own `Pinger`; fixing them here would
duplicate `icmp`'s internal header parsing rather than close the gap at its source. Out of scope:
parallel/all-hops-at-once probing, the TCP trace method, non-Linux live path, MTU/PMTU discovery.

## Verification
Offline-first: the hop state machine runs against a fake transport that builds canned RFC 792-shaped
response bytes (Time Exceeded, Echo Reply, Destination Unreachable, drops, late replies, load-
balanced hops, malformed/hostile input) through the real `icmp.echo` parsers on a deterministic
virtual clock — TTL/ident/seq stamping, terminal-code handling, `*` timeouts, `distinctAddresses`,
per-hop `latency-stats`, IPv4 raw-header shape, IPv6, option validation. One live test traces
`127.0.0.1`, skipped without CAP_NET_RAW. Run: `zig build test-traceroute`.

**2026-10-04:** real kernel replies to UDP probes from a veth router sandbox (client → router →
server in three throwaway netns inside `unshare -rnm`, tcpdump-decoded): the router's Time
Exceeded and the server's Port Unreachable drive a two-hop UDP trace to `reached`; the same bytes
are refused under a wrong source port, a port window that excludes them, a different destination,
a quoted protocol other than UDP and a damaged ICMP checksum; the server's Port Unreachable from
the router's address is terminal, not `reached`; a late duplicate does not overwrite a slot. An
MPLS-extended Time Exceeded that tcpdump decodes ("checksum … (correct)", "label 16, tc 0, ttl 1")
yields its two-entry stack; each RFC 4884 rule (128-byte minimum, version 2, C-Type 1, the
compatibility checksum) is shown rejecting on its own with every checksum valid. IPv6 UDP uses
code 4. Live (CAP_NET_RAW): a UDP trace to 127.0.0.1 ends on the loopback's Port Unreachable,
and `iface`/`source`/`tos` are read back off the sockets. Mutation 2026-10-04: 29 mutants, all
killed.

## Backlog / deferred
Documented out-of-scope: parallel probing, UDP/TCP methods, non-Linux live path,
MTU/PMTU discovery (the first two now also filed below from the survey).
- **2026-10-04:** UDP method, ICMP extensions/MPLS and source/interface/TOS are **done** (see
  "UDP method, extensions, live options"). Still deferred: **TCP** (needs SYN probes on a raw TCP
  socket or connect()-per-probe, and RST/SYN-ACK matching — a separate receive path; no consumer
  asks), **parallel probing** (a window in the state machine; worth doing with a consumer that
  traces many destinations), **Paris/Dublin** (flow-stable UDP needs a constant 5-tuple, i.e. the
  probe id carried in the checksum/payload — builds on the UDP method, now possible), RFC 5837
  interface-information objects.
- **UDP and TCP probe methods** (survey 2026-09-30): traceroute(8)'s default is UDP and it offers TCP; trippy does ICMP/UDP/TCP. A user behind a firewall that drops ICMP echo gets a wall of `*`. Effort: medium (per-method probe encoding and matching the quoted transport header; the SPEC notes the quoted header is currently discarded by `icmp.echo`). Fits CONVENTIONS §2 (raw sockets via `std.os.linux`).
- **Parallel probing** (survey 2026-09-30): sequential by design today (one probe in flight); a 30-hop trace across silent hops costs up to 30×probes×timeout. traceroute(8) and mtr send concurrently. Effort: medium (slot scheme already correlates late replies, so the state machine mostly needs a window). Fits §2.
- **Multipath-aware strategy (Paris/Dublin-style flow-stable probes)** (survey 2026-09-30): per-flow load balancers make classic traceroute show false paths; trippy implements the two strategies. Effort: medium-large, depends on the UDP/TCP methods above. Fits §2.
- **ICMP extension objects / MPLS labels (RFC 4884/4950)** (survey 2026-09-30): traceroute(8) prints them *(inferred)*; needs the quoted-datagram parsing that `icmp.echo` currently drops. Effort: medium, partly in `icmp`. Fits §2.
- **Source-address / interface / TOS options on the live path** (survey 2026-09-30): multi-homed hosts cannot pick the egress; `icmp.Pinger` has `iface`/`oiface`/`tos`. Effort: small. Fits §2.

## Status
`gap · linux · client · single_owner` + deps: `icmp`, `netaddr`, `latency-stats` — canonical source
is `pub const meta` in src/root.zig.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — every path's expected values come from an implementation that is not ours.

**What the tests actually contain.** src/kernel_oracle_test.zig replays 16 live traces against real Linux routers (`tools/interop.zig` + `tools/kernel_oracle.py` → `kernel_oracle_vectors.zig`): a client → r1 → r2 → r3 → server chain of network namespaces per scenario — clean, r2 dropping its own Time Exceeded, r3 rejecting with Administratively Prohibited, the server dropping everything — for the ICMP and the UDP method over IPv4 and IPv6. The transport was recorded (every probe sent, every packet or timeout received, on a virtual clock); `traceWith` must send the same probes in the same order and report the same trace, and every hop is what the topology puts at that TTL — each router's client-side address, `*` for the silent one, `!X` (code 13 / v6 code 1) from the filter, the server's Echo Reply / Port Unreachable — which traceroute(8) 2.1.6 traced identically. The real tcpdump-decoded captures below anchor the refusal rules (wrong port, destination, protocol, checksum) and the RFC 4884/4950 extension parsing. Self only: the canned-fixture tests of hostile input, which have no outside answer

**Kernel oracle 2026-10-05.** One defect, fixed the same day: a terminal hop (Destination Unreachable) stopped after its first probe and reported the unsent rest as `.timeout` — a `*`, and a loss in `Hop.stats`, where traceroute(8) shows `!X` for every probe. It now sends the hop's full count, as it always did for the destination's hop.

**How it got there.** The anchoring work landed. DONE 466cc70: real 2-hop veth router; Time Exceeded from a real TTL decrement
